column1: Questionnaire
Does the vendor have a formal security governance framework?
Is there a dedicated security team or officer responsible for cybersecurity?
Does the vendor conduct security risk assessments at least annually?
Are security policies reviewed and updated periodically?
Does the vendor have a formal security awareness training program?
Does your company have a dedicated, full-time employee or subcontracted IT staff?
Does your company has a dedicated, full-time employee or subcontracted cyber security staff?
Does your company have a cyber security user education and awareness program?
Does your company perform phishing email testing of its employees?
Is the vendor compliant with industry security standards (ISO 27001, SOC 2, etc.)?
Does the vendor have a legal framework for handling customer data securely?

Does your company perform cyber security audits by objective internal employees or external 3rd parties on IT systems/devices and IT services that store or process sensitive information at least annually?
Does the vendor have data protection agreements with sub-processors?
Does the vendor comply with data privacy regulations like DPDP/ISO 27701, etc.?
Does your company have a Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT) with a formal process to respond to cyber attacks?
Are encryption mechanisms in place for data at rest and in transit?
Does the vendor implement data loss prevention (DLP) controls?
Are data backup and restoration processes tested regularly?
Does the vendor enforce secure data disposal practices?
Are there access restrictions for handling sensitive customer data?
Does your company perform full packet capture?

Does your company protect sensitive information received from a third-party company during transmission between the owning third-party as well as other parties with whom that data is shared (i.e. Encryption, SSL/TLS connections)?
Do all devices that store or process sensitive information at a minimum have commercially available antivirus with current signature files?

Do all devices that store or process sensitive information at a minimum have all unnecessary ports and services disabled and the device is used for limited functions (ex. A device acting solely as a file server vs. a file server, FTP server, and web server)?

Are all laptop devices that store sensitive information encrypted?
Note: For IT environments with no laptop devices.

Do all mobile devices (e.g. Smartphone’s, tablets) that store sensitive information at a minimum have configuration management provided by a company owned centrally managed infrastructure?
Note: For IT environments with no mobile devices
Does the vendor have firewalls, IDS/IPS, and endpoint security measures?
Are security patches applied regularly and within SLA timelines?
Does the vendor have a secure software development lifecycle (SDLC)?
Are vulnerability scans and penetration testing performed regularly?

Do all mobile devices (e.g. smartphones, tablets) that store sensitive information at a minimum have the ability to remotely wipe the device?
Note: For IT environments with no mobile devices
Does the vendor implement logging and monitoring for security events?

Does your company require 2-factor authentication for remote access (e.g. token used in addition to a username and password for VPN login)?
Note: For IT environments with no remote access
Do all devices that store or process sensitive information at a minimum have a unique user name and complex password to access the system?
Do all devices that store or process sensitive information at a minimum has access control that is configured on a least privilege model (a person only has access to the data/device that they need)?

Do all mobile devices (e.g. Smartphone’s, tablets) that store sensitive information at a minimum have access control to the device (complex password to access device)?
Note: For IT environments with no mobile devices
Does the vendor have role-based access control (RBAC) implemented?
Are privileged accounts monitored and reviewed periodically?
Does the vendor enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA)?
Is there a formal process for granting and revoking access?
Are user access logs maintained and reviewed regularly?
Does the vendor have an incident response plan?
Are security incidents documented and analyzed for future improvements?
Does the vendor have a dedicated incident response team?
Has the vendor conducted incident response drills in the past year?
Are customers notified of security incidents in a timely manner?
Does the vendor have a business continuity and disaster recovery (BC/DR) plan?
Is the BC/DR plan tested at least annually?
Are critical business functions identified and prioritized?
Are alternate data centers or recovery sites available?
Does your company have capabilities of detecting and blocking malicious email prior to delivery to the end user?

Does your company control web access based on the risk (e.g. reputation, content, and security) of the sites being visited (e.g. Web Proxy Controls)?
Note: For IT environments with no Internet connection

Do all devices that store or process sensitive information at a minimum have vulnerability scanning performed at least monthly AND are vulnerabilities being remediated in a risk based priority (highest priority vulnerabilities are fixed first)?
Does the vendor conduct periodic risk assessments for business continuity?
